---
title: "sapply() is a loop, and ifelse() computes everything"
ref: DF-09
categories: [Data frames and lists]
impact: incoherent
attendu: "a single vectorised call, and no warning for the negative values"
versions: "All"
source: "The R Inferno"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
calls <- 0
square <- function(v) {
  calls <<- calls + 1
  v^2
}
res <- sapply(1:1000, square)
calls

x <- c(-1, 10)
ifelse(x > 0, yes = log(x), no = NA)
```
:::

## Why

The functions of the `apply` family hide a loop: `sapply()` calls the function once per element, here a thousand times. That is not vectorisation. When the function already knows how to work on a whole vector, like `^`, wrapping it in `sapply()` only slows things down.

Conversely, vectorising at all costs has a price too. `ifelse()` computes both of its branches in full, then picks element by element. So `log(x)` is computed for -1 as well, hence the warning, even though the condition was meant to rule that case out. On heavy computations, you pay for every branch on every value.

## The fix

Call the vectorised functions directly, and keep the computation for the elements that need it.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
calls <- 0
res2 <- square(1:1000)
calls
identical(res, y = res2)

result <- rep(NA_real_, times = length(x))
positive <- x > 0
result[positive] <- log(x[positive])
result
```
:::
